sql.what: Querying the product's data yourself: joins, aggregations, window functions, and knowing where the tables are and what they mean.

subskills.name: Joins & aggregations
subskills.example: Join events to accounts and count weekly active accounts by plan.

subskills.name: Window functions & cohorts
subskills.example: Compute week-N retention per signup cohort in one query.

subskills.name: Knowing the schema
subskills.example: Know which table is the source of truth for revenue and its known quirks.

ladder.associate: Writes simple queries against existing tables.
ladder.mid: Answers their own questions with joins, cohorts, and funnels.
ladder.senior: Writes complex analyses; spots data-quality issues in the warehouse.
ladder.lead: Rarely queries; ensures the team can and the data is trustworthy.

build: Course: Mode's SQL tutorial or 'SQL for Data Analysis' (free); practice on real-looking datasets.
Project: load a public dataset into SQLite or DuckDB and answer ten product questions.
At work: get warehouse access and answer one question a week without an analyst.
signals: Self-serve SQL for all funnel and retention analysis; no analyst dependency.
Built the dbt model for weekly active workspaces used by the whole org.

python_r.what: Scripting for analysis and prototyping: cleaning data, building quick models, automating the repetitive.

subskills.name: Data wrangling (pandas / tidyverse)
subskills.example: Clean a 200k-row export and build a cohort table in a notebook.

subskills.name: Notebooks & visualization
subskills.example: A notebook that regenerates the weekly analysis with one run.

subskills.name: Scripting & automation
subskills.example: A script that pulls the metrics and posts the digest to Slack.

subskills.name: Prototyping with code
subskills.example: A Streamlit prototype that shows the idea before engineering invests.

ladder.associate: Can run and modify an existing notebook.
ladder.mid: Writes analysis scripts and small prototypes independently.
ladder.senior: Builds internal tools and models; prototypes AI features end to end.
ladder.lead: Uses code to stay close to the product; sets expectations for technical PMs.

build: Course: 'Python for Everybody' then a pandas course; or R for Data Science (free online book).
Project: automate a weekly report you'd otherwise do by hand.
At work: prototype the next idea in a notebook before writing the spec.
signals: Built a Python pipeline that automated the weekly cohort report (saved 4h/week).
Prototyped the recommendation feature in a notebook; shipped version matched it within 5%.

data_modeling.what: Understanding how data is structured, moved, and governed: pipelines, warehouses, schemas, quality, and ownership.

subskills.name: Pipelines & ETL/ELT
subskills.example: Know when the nightly job runs and what breaks downstream if it fails.

subskills.name: Schema & data modelling
subskills.example: Define the events and entities before engineering picks a table design.

subskills.name: Data quality & governance
subskills.example: Assign an owner and a freshness SLA to every core table.

subskills.name: Warehouse & lakehouse platforms
subskills.example: Understand cost and latency trade-offs between warehouse and lake.

ladder.associate: Knows where the data comes from and who owns it.
ladder.mid: Writes tracking plans and partners with data engineering on models.
ladder.senior: Owns data products or platforms; sets governance for an area.
ladder.lead: Sets data strategy; owns the data platform roadmap.

build: Course: a data engineering fundamentals course (the dbt Learn courses are free).
Project: design the schema and pipeline for an analytics product; draw the lineage.
At work: own the tracking plan and the data contract for your feature.
signals: Owned the customer data platform roadmap; cut pipeline failures 70%.
Designed the event schema that unified mobile and web analytics.

technical_fluency.what: Understanding how software is built well enough to make good trade-offs with engineers, without needing to write the code yourself.

subskills.name: Technical trade-offs
subskills.example: Decide whether to pay down the migration now or ship the feature first, with eyes open.

subskills.name: Reading code & systems
subskills.example: Read the PR to check the edge case is handled instead of asking.

subskills.name: How the system works
subskills.example: Draw the request path from the client to the database for your feature.

subskills.name: Engineering partnership
subskills.example: Run planning with the tech lead as a peer, not a ticket taker.

ladder.associate: Understands the stack at a block-diagram level; asks good questions.
ladder.mid: Discusses trade-offs with engineers credibly; reads code when needed.
ladder.senior: Shapes technical direction with the tech lead; anticipates platform needs.
ladder.lead: Partners with engineering leadership on architecture investments.

build: Course: CS50 or 'How the Internet Works' level fundamentals; then a system design primer.
Project: build and deploy a small app (any stack) so you've touched every layer once.
At work: shadow an engineer for a sprint; draw the architecture of your product.
signals: Led the build-vs-buy decision for the search service with engineering.
CS background; regularly reads PRs and participates in design reviews.

apis.what: Designing and managing APIs and integrations as products: developer experience, versioning, docs, and the ecosystem that builds on them.

subskills.name: API design
subskills.example: Design the resource model and review the OpenAPI spec before build.

subskills.name: Developer experience & docs
subskills.example: Measure time-to-first-successful-call and get it under 10 minutes.

subskills.name: Versioning & deprecation
subskills.example: Ship v2 with a migration guide and keep v1 alive for 12 months.

subskills.name: Integrations & webhooks
subskills.example: Prioritize the five integrations that unblock the most deals.

subskills.name: API adoption & reliability
subskills.example: Track active API keys, error rates, and p95 latency per endpoint.

ladder.associate: Writes clear integration docs; understands the API surface.
ladder.mid: Owns an API or integration; runs the design review and docs.
ladder.senior: Owns the developer platform; sets versioning and DX standards.

build: Course: an API design course (Google's API design guide is free; Stripe's docs are the model).
Project: design an API for a small product: resources, endpoints, errors, a quick-start doc.
At work: own the docs and versioning policy for one API.
signals: Owned the public API; active integrations grew from 80 to 400.
Led the v2 API migration with zero forced breakages for 300 partners.

system_architecture.what: Understanding how large systems are structured and why: services, data stores, scaling limits, reliability, and what changes cost.

subskills.name: Distributed systems basics
subskills.example: Know why eventual consistency means the dashboard lags by a minute.

subskills.name: Scalability & performance
subskills.example: Ask what breaks at 10× traffic before promising it to sales.

subskills.name: Reliability & resilience
subskills.example: Set an SLO with engineering and decide what gets cut when it's breached.

subskills.name: Platform & internal tools
subskills.example: Decide what belongs in the platform versus the product team's code.

ladder.associate: Can read an architecture diagram and explain the main components.
ladder.mid: Discusses scaling and reliability trade-offs for their feature.
ladder.senior: Shapes platform roadmaps; owns SLOs and capacity decisions with engineering.
ladder.lead: Partners with engineering leadership on multi-year architecture bets.

build: Read: 'Designing Data-Intensive Applications' (the first half is enough); the System Design Primer on GitHub.
Project: draw the architecture of a product you use and guess where it would fail at scale.
At work: attend architecture reviews and write up the trade-offs in plain English.
signals: Owned the platform roadmap during the move to microservices; p95 latency down 60%.
Defined SLOs for the payments service and the error budget policy.

cloud.what: Working knowledge of cloud platforms: core services, cost, and how infrastructure choices shape the product.

subskills.name: Core cloud services
subskills.example: Know which services the product runs on and what each costs.

subskills.name: Containers & orchestration
subskills.example: Understand what a deployment is and why a rollout can be partial.

subskills.name: Cloud cost & FinOps
subskills.example: Own cost per active user and review it monthly.

subskills.name: Cloud certification / depth
subskills.example: Cloud Practitioner or Fundamentals certs cover the vocabulary fast.

ladder.associate: Knows the main services the product uses.
ladder.mid: Understands infra choices and costs for their feature.
ladder.senior: Owns a cloud or infra product, or the cost model for a product.
ladder.lead: Sets infra and platform strategy with engineering.

build: Course: AWS Cloud Practitioner or Azure Fundamentals (free prep material, cheap exams).
Project: deploy a small app to a cloud provider and read the bill.
At work: build the cloud cost model for your product area.
signals: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner; owned the migration PRD to managed Kubernetes.
Cut cloud spend 25% through right-sizing and a reserved-capacity plan.

ai_ml.what: Understanding how machine learning products work: data, models, evaluation, and the product decisions that differ from deterministic software.

subskills.name: ML fundamentals
subskills.example: Know what the model is predicting, from what data, and how it was labelled.

subskills.name: Model evaluation & metrics
subskills.example: Choose precision over recall for the fraud flag and explain why.

subskills.name: ML product design
subskills.example: Design for the 10% of cases where the model is wrong.

subskills.name: ML lifecycle & MLOps
subskills.example: Plan for retraining and drift monitoring before launch, not after.

subskills.name: Recommendations, ranking & search
subskills.example: Define relevance for your users and the offline metric that approximates it.

ladder.associate: Understands what the model does and reads its metrics.
ladder.mid: Writes specs for ML features including evaluation and failure handling.
ladder.senior: Owns ML products; partners with research on what to build and how to evaluate it.
ladder.lead: Sets AI strategy and the bar for responsible deployment.

build: Course: Andrew Ng's 'AI for Everyone', then 'Machine Learning Specialization' if you want depth.
Project: build a small classifier on a public dataset and write up the product decisions it forces.
At work: own the evaluation plan for the next ML feature.
signals: Owned the ranking model roadmap; click-through up 14% with a new evaluation framework.
Designed the human-in-the-loop review flow for low-confidence predictions.

genai_llm.what: Building products on large language models and agents: prompting, retrieval, evaluation, cost, safety, and the new UX patterns they need.

subskills.name: Prompt design & context engineering
subskills.example: Write and version the system prompt like code; test it on a fixed set.

subskills.name: Retrieval & grounding (RAG)
subskills.example: Decide what to retrieve, how to chunk it, and how to show sources.

subskills.name: Evals & quality
subskills.example: Build a 200-example golden set and run it on every prompt change.

subskills.name: Agents & tool use
subskills.example: Scope which actions the agent can take alone and which need approval.

subskills.name: Cost, latency & model selection
subskills.example: Route simple requests to a small model; measure cost per task.

subskills.name: Safety, guardrails & trust
subskills.example: Define failure modes, add guardrails, and red-team before launch.

subskills.name: AI UX patterns
subskills.example: Show sources, allow edits, collect thumbs-down reasons.

ladder.associate: Has built something with an LLM API; understands prompts and limits.
ladder.mid: Ships LLM features with an eval set, guardrails, and cost tracking.
ladder.senior: Owns an AI product line; sets evaluation and safety standards.
ladder.lead: Sets AI strategy; decides build vs. API vs. fine-tune at the company level.

build: Course: DeepLearning.AI's short courses (prompting, RAG, evals, agents) are free and practical.
Project: build a RAG app over documents you know, with a 50-example eval set, and write up what failed.
At work: own the eval set and the guardrail spec for an AI feature.
signals: Shipped the AI assistant to 50k users; built the eval harness that gates every prompt change.
Cut inference cost 60% with model routing while holding quality on a 300-case golden set.

mobile.what: Building for iOS and Android: platform conventions, app store rules, release cycles, and the constraints of the device.

subskills.name: Platform conventions
subskills.example: Follow platform navigation patterns instead of porting the web UI.

subskills.name: App store & release
subskills.example: Plan around review times and a two-week release train.

subskills.name: Device constraints
subskills.example: Design the offline state before the happy path.

subskills.name: Mobile growth & analytics
subskills.example: Track crash-free sessions and day-1/7/30 retention per release.

ladder.associate: Knows the release process and store requirements.
ladder.mid: Owns a mobile feature end to end including the release.
ladder.senior: Owns a mobile app or platform area; sets quality and release standards.

build: Course: an intro iOS or Android development course (even a weekend one) to feel the constraints.
Project: ship a tiny app to TestFlight or an internal track.
At work: own a mobile release end to end, including the store listing.
signals: Owned the Android app; crash-free sessions from 97.2% to 99.6%, rating 3.8 to 4.5.
Shipped offline mode used by 30% of field users.

security_privacy.what: Building products that protect users and data: threat models, access control, privacy by design, and compliance obligations.

subskills.name: Threat modelling
subskills.example: List how a feature could be abused before it ships.

subskills.name: Identity & access
subskills.example: Design roles and permissions that map to how customers actually organize.

subskills.name: Privacy by design
subskills.example: Collect the minimum, define retention, and build deletion in from day one.

subskills.name: Compliance frameworks
subskills.example: Know which controls your feature touches and who signs off.

subskills.name: Trust, safety & fraud
subskills.example: Define the fraud signals and the manual review path.

ladder.associate: Follows security review processes; understands PII handling.
ladder.mid: Runs threat models and privacy reviews for their features.
ladder.senior: Owns security or identity products, or the security posture of an area.
ladder.lead: Sets security and privacy strategy with the CISO.

build: Course: an intro to application security (OWASP Top 10) and a privacy fundamentals module (IAPP).
Project: threat-model a feature of an app you use and write the mitigations.
At work: run the security and privacy review for your next feature yourself.
signals: Owned enterprise identity (SSO, SCIM, RBAC); unblocked $6M in enterprise deals.
Led SOC 2 Type II readiness for the product; zero findings.

devops_sdlc.what: How software gets from commit to production and stays healthy: CI/CD, releases, observability, and incident response.

subskills.name: Observability & monitoring

subskills.name: Incident response & postmortems

subskills.name: SDLC & engineering process
subskills.example: Understand what 'done' means at each stage from PR to production.

ladder.associate: Understands the release process and reads incident updates.
ladder.mid: Participates in incidents and postmortems for their area.
ladder.senior: Owns reliability goals for a product; shapes release and on-call practices with engineering.
ladder.lead: Partners with engineering leadership on engineering effectiveness.

build: Read: 'Accelerate' (DORA metrics) and the Google SRE book's early chapters.
Project: set up CI and a deploy pipeline for a small project.
At work: join the on-call channel; own comms for one incident.
signals: Owned the release train; deploy frequency up 3×, change failure rate down 40%.
Ran customer comms and the postmortem for the March outage.

hardware.what: Building physical products or the software on them: development phases, manufacturing, firmware, and the long lead times involved.

subskills.example: Plan OTA updates and rollback from the start.

subskills.name: Testing, certification & quality
subskills.example: Schedule certification into the timeline; it doesn't compress.

subskills.name: Silicon & compute platforms
subskills.example: Understand roadmap dependencies on the chip vendor's schedule.

ladder.associate: Understands the build phases and tracks schedule.
ladder.mid: Owns requirements for a subsystem through EVT to production.
ladder.senior: Owns a hardware product line; manages cost, schedule, and quality trade-offs.
ladder.lead: Sets hardware roadmap and platform strategy.
